boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Dayton, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daytime-to-evening first-weekend loop through named University of Dayton spaces for orienting yourself, studying, moving, reflecting and seeing campus arts.

cards.title: Start with the campus chapel
cards.subtitle: A quiet first landmark near the center of campus
cards.notes: Walk through the entrance plaza, look for the stained glass, and pause respectfully before continuing your orientation loop.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark suited to a calm first stop.
cards.evidence_claim: UD describes the Chapel of the Immaculate Conception as the heart of its community since its 1869 construction and invites people to seek it out for quiet prayer.
cards.source_title: Chapel of the Immaculate Conception | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: Use it as a place of worship and reflection; respect any services or reserved activity in progress.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Kennedy Union
cards.subtitle: Campus services and gathering space
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical checkpoint: locate posted information, meet a new classmate, and plan the next stop together.
cards.short_summary: A central union for services and informal meetups.
cards.evidence_claim: UD says Kennedy Memorial Union offers comfortable surroundings and a variety of services for the University community.
cards.access_notes: Check the building's current postings and desk information for available services and spaces.

cards.title: Choose a Roesch Library study spot
cards.subtitle: Library study spaces and services
cards.notes: Take a short reconnaissance lap, then settle into a space matching your group’s noise level and study plans for the week.
cards.short_summary: A flexible stop for learning the campus library’s study options.
cards.evidence_claim: UD says Roesch Library provides spaces designed for different preferences, including solo and group work, silent study and busier settings.
cards.source_title: University Libraries Visit | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: Some reservable spaces require a UD email address; review library guidance before reserving one.

cards.title: Map out the week at Gathering Place
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Roesch Library
cards.notes: Bring calendars or syllabi and make a simple plan with friends, leaving time to identify library help and course deadlines.
cards.short_summary: An active, flexible second-floor library area.
cards.evidence_claim: UD identifies Gathering Place as an open second-floor area in Roesch Library that is typically arranged for active, flexible study.
cards.source_title: University Libraries Visit | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: This area can be reserved for events, so confirm availability when you arrive.

cards.title: See the Marian Library collection
cards.subtitle: Seventh floor of Roesch Library
cards.notes: Visit during public hours to view a specialized campus collection, and plan ahead if you need staff assistance or an appointment.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing specialized library within Roesch.
cards.evidence_claim: UD states that the Marian Library is on Roesch Library’s seventh floor and is open to the public Tuesday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Marian Library Hours and Location | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Tuesday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; Monday visits are by appointment.

cards.title: Fit in a RecPlex reset
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation at 2 Evanston Ave.
cards.notes: Bring your valid ID, check current facility access, and choose a low-key movement break before returning to the rest of campus.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop for an active afternoon break.
cards.evidence_claim: UD identifies the RecPlex as its campus recreation hub and states that members must present a valid University ID or Campus Recreation membership card.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Hours, Policies and FAQ | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid University ID or Campus Recreation membership card; facility hours and construction notices can change.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk by Stuart Field
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation field
cards.notes: Use the field perimeter for a daylight stroll and conversation, while giving scheduled practices, clubs, and reserved activities space.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor recreation-field stop during operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: UD lists Stuart Field’s regular operating hours as dawn to dusk on weekdays and 9 a.m. to dusk on weekends, subject to reserved events.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Hours, Policies and FAQ | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are dawn–dusk weekdays and 9 a.m.–dusk weekends; access may be limited by scheduled events.

cards.title: Explore ArtStreet’s creative spaces
cards.subtitle: South Student Neighborhood arts complex
cards.notes: Walk through the complex, notice the studios and amphitheatre, and check campus channels for student-organization activities or reservations.
cards.short_summary: A named student-neighborhood complex with arts and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UD says ArtStreet includes studios for academic courses and student organizations, the Brook Center, a student-run café and an outdoor amphitheatre.
cards.access_notes: Some spaces are used by courses or organizations and may require a reservation to use.

cards.entity_name: Roger Glass Center for the Arts
cards.title: Visit the Glass Center gallery
cards.subtitle: Visual and performing arts center
cards.notes: Check the events listing, then visit the lobby and gallery during public building hours or attend an appropriately scheduled arts event.
cards.short_summary: A modern campus arts destination with public gallery access.
cards.evidence_claim: UD describes the Roger Glass Center for the Arts as its first dedicated visual and performing arts building, hosting performances and visual-art exhibits.
cards.source_title: Roger Glass Center for the Arts | University of Dayton
cards.access_notes: During fall and spring terms, the lobby and gallery list public hours of 10 a.m.–8 p.m. Monday–Friday; event hours can extend beyond that.

cards.title: End with a historic campus landmark
cards.subtitle: Historic University of Dayton building
cards.notes: Take an exterior look at St. Mary’s Hall and connect the weekend’s new campus map to the university’s earliest physical history.
cards.short_summary: A National Register-listed historic building on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UD says St. Mary’s Hall opened in 1871 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior landmark stop and follow posted building-access guidance.
